figures.caption: Figure 2A1 shows average sucrose, NaCl, and quinine lick cluster sizes for a 100 pair of representative rats’ initial BAT sessions. While both rats produced very small lick 101 clusters when offered the bitter quinine, and both produced large lick clusters when 102 offered NaCl, they differed notably in their sucrose cluster sizes. A 2-way ANOVA of 103 these data revealed a significant rat x taste interaction (F(2,65)=13.44, p < 0.001), with 104 one of the two rats preferring sucrose to NaCl (p < 0.05) and the other showing little 105 sign even of preference for sucrose over quinine (p > 0.05). 106 Even casual scrutiny of Figure 2A2, which presents lick cluster sizes to every 107 taste across all 9 rats (the red dashed box delineates the rats used for Figure 2A1) 108 suggests that while few of the 5 rats that sampled sucrose didn’t like sucrose, individual 109 variability was large enough that individual preference orders often diverged from the 110 canonical palatability ranking (in the case of the battery used with subjects R4, R5, R6, 111 R7, R8, and R9, this canonical ordering was sucrose > NaCl > citric acid > quinine). 112 While the precise battery offered varied from rat to rat, each offered easy canonical 113 ordering (see Table 1 for canonical rankings of each battery), and in many cases actual 114 individual rats’ preferences differed from this ordering. 115 These differences were easily observed in a comparison of lick cluster sizes to 116 sucrose and NaCl (typically the most palatable tastes) in rats that sampled both (Figure 117 2A3-top), which makes it clear that some rats prefer (this concentration of) NaCl over 118 (this concentration of) sucrose, while others do not. Similarly, differences between citric 119 acid and quinine (both typically thought of as aversive tastes) lick cluster sizes (Figure 120 2A3-bottom) revealed individual differences in how aversive each was to rats that 121 sampled both: some rats disliked quinine more than citric acid whereas several did not. 122 These impressions were statistically confirmed using one-sample t-tests against a null 123

Figure 2. Individual and between-session differences in perceived taste585 palatability. (A1-3) Data from first BAT sessions (B1-3) Data from final BAT sessions.586 (A1) Mean lick cluster sizes for two representative rats during the first BAT test illustrate587 clear individual differences in preference for sucrose, NaCl, and QHCl. A two-way588 ANOVA revealed a significant Taste × Animal interaction (F(2,65) = 13.44, p < 0.05).589 Post hoc Tukey tests further showed that sucrose, while highly preferred by the rat on590 the left, was perceived similarly to QHCl by the rat on the right (p < 0.05). (A2) Mean lick591 cluster sizes for each taste across all animals during the first BAT test (N = 9). The two592 rats shown in panel (A1) are outlined for reference. (A3) Differences in lick cluster sizes593 comparing sucrose and NaCl (top) and comparing citric acid (CA) and quinine (QHCl;594 bottom) during the first BAT test. One-sample t-tests (against a population mean of595 zero) revealed individual differences in the preferences for the two palatable and the596 two aversive tastes (p < 0.05). (B1-3) The same analyses as in A1-3, but for each rat’s597 final BAT session (depending on the rat, sessions 3 or 5). In (B3), we also show an598 analysis of whether individual rats changed their relative preferences between BAT599 sessions—two-way ANOVAs with variables Animal and Session, comparing the data600 shown in panels (A3) and (B3). The majority of rats exhibited significant changes in601 relative preference for tastes of the same valence across sessions (#, ps < 0.05). The602 labels R1–R9 denote the rats included in the data analysis. 603

Figure 3. Experience-related changes in taste preferences are not attenuation of605 neophobia. Each panel shows the change in lick bout lengths between the first to final606 BAT session for either palatable (left) or aversive (right) tastes. In both cases,607 experience clearly changes behavior, but the changes aren’t in a consistent direction.608 See text for details. 609
